summary: Chased the one caveat left in the vote-durability account and corrected it. The logdb state cache is updated while the write batch is still being assembled, so a failed commit would leave it claiming a state that never reached disk; what actually closes the window is the engine's only call site, which panics on a raft state write error, so no live process can observe the stale cache and a new process rebuilds it from disk. The vote interpretation now states that mechanism instead of the earlier assumption that the cache holds only committed states, records the cache ordering as a Behavior, and marks both open questions (vote durability, restart anchor) as explained with their discriminators cleared.
